summary: Rogue River NF lookout on Steve Peak: a fire destroyed the station in 1918, a 12x12 cab followed in 1919, and the L-5 tower was removed in 1968.

facts.design: 12x12 cab (1919), later a 20-foot pole L-5 tower
facts.status_note: L-5 tower removed in 1968 (firelookout.com says destroyed); the register lists it among former lookout sites

staffing.status: observer posted by 1916; a lookout was on the station in August 1918; no later staffing dates in these sources

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Rogue River National Forest)

events.note: District fire plan proposed a lookoutman on Steve's Peak and a spur line to its top; a plan only, not confirmed as built
Observer's camp with a call bell; the observer could be called to the phone when not on top
Dr. Barker, a retired Jacksonville physician, was the lookout when the fire came in August
Fire reached the lookout station just after Dr. Barker left, destroying it and its contents (Medford Mail Tribune)
12x12 cab, per the register and firelookout.com
Camp Applegate CCC crews started work on the lookout in September; the register dates the 20-foot L-5 tower only to the 1930s
L-5 tower removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.quote: A 12'x12' cab built in 1919 was replaced in the 1930s with a 20' pole L-5 tower, which was removed in 1968.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1918 Medford Mail Tribune item says the fire destroyed the lookout station, while the register dates the 12x12 cab to 1919. No source says whether the 1919 cab replaced the station that burned.
The register says the tower was removed in 1968; firelookout.com says it was destroyed. Both agree on the year.

sources.title: Steve Peak Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites register

notes_for_editor: Only the Oregon Lookouts page carries a timeline (it runs 1913 to a September 1933 CCC item, then a bare 'Removed' tag with no date). It quotes Medford Mail Tribune items and Forest history volumes, which were not read in original form. The 1918 fire versus 1919 cab question is open and the story says so. Two searches found no post-1933 history and no description of the site today. No access information found. Confidence is medium because the only timeline is one compiled page.
